subject: SOC 2 Type II - cut-off inclusivity & delayed-ingest exceptions
messages:
From: Ian Murray <ian@auditpoint.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: FinEx Security Team <security@finex.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: SOC 2 Type II - cut-off and ingest timing question

Hi Laura,

Quick question as we prepare the fieldwork for Redwood's upcoming Type II report: for the period ending 2026-07-31, does Redwood treat the final day inclusively as up to 2026-07-31T23:59:59 UTC (i.e., as-of coverage) or are some control evidences captured as an interval where the last moment is exclusive?

Separately, we understand some of your telemetry pipelines perform delayed ingestion (up to ~48 hours) for certain services. For the audit, will you be providing evidence stamped by event_time, or will you be relying on ingestion_time snapshots? If you use event_time for some systems and ingest_time for others, please indicate which systems fall into each bucket.

If there are known delayed-ingest exceptions (e.g., delayed logs arriving after the period boundary), would Redwood expect to provide a bridge letter describing the exception handling and the compensating evidence? If so, does Redwood have a standard draft?

Can you share a sample list of system evidence and the expected cut-off rule for each? If helpful, we can set a short call this afternoon.

Thanks,
Ian
Ian Murray
Senior Manager, AuditPoint
ian@auditpoint.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ian Murray <ian@auditpoint.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, FinEx Security Team <security@finex.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II - cut-off and ingest timing question

Thanks for the clear questions, Ian — copying Marissa (Product Security) and Karthik (Infra) so we can provide specifics. High-level answers below, with examples and next steps. Attached: log-retention-manifest.pdf (inventory) and a working bridge letter draft (bridge-draft.docx).

1) Cut-off inclusivity: canonical rule is that the audit period is inclusive through 2026-07-31T23:59:59 UTC for event-based evidence (we treat event_time <= boundary as in-scope). For systems that only have ingest_time (e.g., third-party partner logs) we treat evidence as in-scope if the ingest_time falls within the period.

2) Event_time vs ingest_time:
- Core runtime (request/response traces, KV-store operations): event_time is authoritative. We extract as-of snapshots keyed to event_time.
- Message queues and partner-forwarded logs: ingest_time only — these are listed in the attached manifest. We log and mark them as ingest-time evidence.

3) Delayed-ingest exceptions: we do have a documented exception process. In practice, delayed items (rare) are either: a) reimported with original event_time preserved (if available), or b) captured as an ingest-time record and flagged for auditors. For records that arrive after the period boundary with event_time within the period, we preserve event_time and include them as retroactive evidence — we’ll annotate these in the evidence manifest.

4) Bridge letter: yes, we generally provide a short bridge letter for any material delayed-ingest handling to explain scope and provide compensating controls (reconciliation jobs, sequence checks). I attached a starting draft; feel free to redline.

Next steps:
- Ian: can you confirm whether AuditPoint prefers (A) strict as-of evidence only, (B) event_time-with-annotation for retroactive arrivals, or (C) ingest_time-by-system (we can provide mapping)?
- Marissa/Karthik: please review the attached manifest and mark any systems that cannot preserve event_time and note typical ingestion delay windows.
- I'll schedule a 30-min sync for 2:30pm PT if that works for audit and FinEx.

Laura Bennett
Director, Compliance & Controls
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II - cut-off and ingest timing question

Laura — thanks, that clear mapping helps. A couple of follow-ups:

- For our report wording, we need explicit confirmation that event_time =< 2026-07-31T23:59:59 UTC is considered in-scope when event_time exists. Can you confirm that as an authoritative statement we can include in the report / management representation?

- For retroactive arrivals where event_time is within the period but ingest_time > period_end, will Redwood produce an annotated manifest entry showing: original event_time, ingest_time, and the sequence id? That will satisfy our sampling and traceability procedures.

- Regarding the bridge letter, I reviewed the draft you attached. It looks fine as a concept — two small asks: (1) a one-line quantification of how often delayed-ingest events occur (e.g., <0.1% of total events for the service) and (2) a bullet listing compensating reconciliation steps. Can you add both?

I can take a quick call at 14:30 PT today to walk through the manifest.

Best,
Ian

I put a few inline suggestions in the Drive doc: https://drive.redwood.com/soc2/2026/bridge-draft

Call scheduled: 2026-08-09 14:30 PT / 21:30 UTC — invite sent. Agenda: manifest walkthrough, annotated sample, finalize bridge wording.

Laura
